author: Bertrand Russell
title: The Problems of Philosophy
edition: London: Williams and Norgate; New York: Henry Holt and Co., 1912, Home University Library of Modern Knowledge. Scan-backed Wikisource transcription. Prose line wrapping is collapsed within retained paragraphs; HTML emphasis becomes plain text. Printed page numbers, navigation, footnote reference markers, and zero-width page-boundary characters are omitted; main-text wording and punctuation are retained. Original verse line breaks are preserved where present. Apparent errors present in the linked transcription are retained rather than silently corrected; this extraction check is not a fresh complete print-image collation. The library text holds Russell's Preface, Chapters I to XV with their printed numbers and titles, and the Bibliographical Note; the series title page, imprint, contents and the book's index are omitted; the author's single footnote is kept, its anchor [1] in Chapter VII and the note after that chapter's text, where the Wikisource transcription lists it. On 2026-11-18 the unread second half of Chapter I and the opening passages of Chapters II, VI (from “It must be conceded”), VII and VIII were collated word by word against the OCR of Internet Archive problemsofphilos00russuoft (this London 1912 edition) and compared with Project Gutenberg 5827: no reading changed; the printed dates’ dashes and “Königsberg” stand as transcribed.

rights.basis: This original English edition was published in 1912, before 1931, and is public domain in the United States as of 2026. The linked scan index identifies the printed edition; no modern editorial material is supplied.

acquisition.method: Wikisource rendered page HTML (index.php action=render) for the main page and its sixteen subpages in printed order: The Problems of Philosophy (for the Preface), /Chapter 1 to /Chapter 15 and /Bibliographical Note (revisions 10776472, 4983373, 4983681, 4983679, 4986625, 4987838, 4987971, 4995436, 11514645, 4996131, 4996387, 4996412, 4997116, 4997120, 4997136, 4997141, 4995648); downloadSha256 is the SHA-256 of the seventeen responses concatenated in that order and downloadUrl the first of them. Only the transcluded scan text is used: Wikisource headers, page-number anchors and zero-width page-boundary characters removed; the title page, imprint and contents of the main page dropped; centred titles became headings; paragraphs and bibliography entries joined with whitespace collapsed; emphasis flattened; footnote calls kept as [n] in Wikisource's per-subpage numbering, attached to the word before them; each subpage's reference list, which the transcription prints after the subpage's text, became one paragraph per note in Project Gutenberg's form [Footnote n: text], its paragraphs and line breaks joined with single spaces (a note that runs on from one scan page to the next is one note, its continuation marker dropped).
